Definition: ; a prolonged form of a primary, but obsolete ὄμω, for which another prolonged form ὀμόω is used in certain tenses; to swear, i.e. take (or declare on) oath:--swear.
BiblicalUsage: Omnyo means to swear, to take an oath. Jesus forbids swearing at all in Matthew 5:34, neither by heaven, for it is God's throne, and Herod swears rashly in Mark 6:23, offering up to half his kingdom. The oath is also God's own: the oath He swore to Abraham in Luke 1:73, and the oath to David in Acts 2:30, that Christ would sit on his throne.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe oaths show what men trust, because a man swears by what he thinks is greater than himself. My position is that God's oath is the one oath that cannot fail, and the promises He swore to Abraham and David are kept in Christ.
